title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv abstract page)
note: Fetched. cs.AI report, v1 5 Aug 2026, v3 13 Aug 2026 (current). Abstract: 41-day live challenge, day-ahead forecast of the 24 hourly values of aggregated German load from ENTSO-E data; pipeline built on spotforecast2-safe with calendar and weather covariates beats the official ENTSO-E day-ahead forecast; small local in-context models (macl2l) competitive with Chronos-2. Leaderboard public.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv full text, version 1)
note: Fetched (version 1). Task: 24 hourly values of ENTSO-E Actual Total Load, country aggregation DE, due 23:59 UTC the day before; ranked by MAE averaged over scored days. Live phase 10 June to 20 July 2026, 41 target days, summer only, three public holidays. 11 student teams, 8 organiser models, the ENTSO-E forecast and two seasonal naives.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv full text, version 1)
note: Reference pipeline (spotoptim lgbm): recursive LightGBM refitted and tuned daily on 3 years of history; 30 exogenous columns: calendar and solar sine/cosine pairs, six holiday and day-type columns, twelve weather variables for one point (Dortmund) from Open-Meteo, archive for history and the weather forecast over the target day. The ENTSO-E forecast is barred as a model input for standard entries.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv full text, version 1)
note: Leaderboard (Table 6), mean MAE in MW over each entry's own days: MACL2L (ENTSO-E) 1137.1 (29 days), MACL2L 1156.0 (26), student team Hot Rod 1227.8 (41), chronos 1345.8 (39), optuna lgbm 1361.1 (39), spotoptim lgbm 1369.1 (35), ENTSO-E baseline 2155.6 (41), weekly seasonal naive 2501.7, daily naive 3994.8. Hot Rod is 43.0% below the ENTSO-E forecast on full coverage.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv full text, version 1)
note: Paired, shared days: spotoptim lgbm 1369.1 vs ENTSO-E forecast 2097.9 MW on 35 days, 34.7% lower, better on 26 of 35 days (paired t-test; p-value lost in the fetched markdown). SpotOptim vs Optuna tuning tied (1369.1 vs 1371.6). In the Holm-corrected 14-entry panel three student teams separate from the ENTSO-E forecast, which itself does not separate from the weekly seasonal naive.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv full text, version 1)
note: Chronos-2 entry: zero-shot, univariate, 180 days of load as context, median of one 24-hour pass, no covariates or calendar. Paired: chronos vs optuna lgbm 1345.8 vs 1361.1 MW on 39 days, p 0.901; chronos vs spotoptim lgbm 1250.4 vs 1369.1 on 35 days, p 0.238. A univariate foundation model ties a daily-retuned tree model that has weather forecasts and calendar.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv full text, version 1)
note: MACL2L: in-context model on 540 to 600 day-rows; plain variant uses renewable-generation forecasts and day-ahead price as covariates, the other adds the ENTSO-E forecast; output blended with ridge, clipped, spike-repaired. MACL2L vs chronos 1156.0 vs 1283.1 MW on 26 days, p 0.218; MACL2L (ENTSO-E) vs spotoptim lgbm 1137.1 vs 1391.9 on 29 days, p 0.019. No architecture, size or code given.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv full text, version 1)
note: Stated limits: 41 summer days, one zone, no winter; entries joined on different dates; carry-forward and joker rules; covariates changed mid-phase (24 to 30 columns). Numbers recomputed from a data bundle shipped with the manuscript; peer reproduction certified for the 11 teams. Engine and tuner AGPL-3.0-or-later. First author develops the packages evaluated. Chronos-2 revision not stated.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv full text, version 3)
note: Fetched (also a research source). Current version, 13 Aug 2026. Results tables and paired numbers are the same as in version 1; the p-values are readable here: pipeline vs ENTSO-E forecast p 0.0001 (35 shared days, 34.7% lower MAE); SpotOptim vs Optuna p 0.98; Hot Rod vs the pipeline p 0.13; chronos vs optuna lgbm p 0.90; MACL2L vs chronos p 0.22.

title: Short-term load forecasting under EU-AI Act Requirements in Safety-Critical Environments (arXiv full text, version 3)
note: Holm-corrected panel of 14 entries on 35 days (student teams, ENTSO-E forecast, two naives): Hot Rod, Team Neura and Das A Team beat the ENTSO-E forecast (adjusted p under 0.0001, 0.0017, 0.016); no other team does. The ENTSO-E forecast is not separable from the weekly seasonal naive (adjusted p 1.0). Organiser models are not in this panel. Version 3 calls MACL2L a small, locally trained model.

title: Structured Priors: Towards an algebra of component priors for prior-data fitted networks (arXiv abstract page)
note: Fetched (also a research source). Single-author preprint by the challenge organiser, 2 Nov 2026: component priors for prior-data fitted networks, with operators implemented in a software package named macl2l; tabular regression benchmarks, no load forecasting. Shows MACL2L belongs to the organiser's own line of work; no repository link or licence on this page.

title: Enhancing energy system models using better load forecasts (Moebius et al., Energy Systems)
note: Research source, not fetched. Earlier study of the ENTSO-E day-ahead load forecast for Germany-Luxembourg, 2016 to 2019: systematic bias, and modelling the forecast error alone removes roughly a fifth of its RMSE. Independent support that the operator forecast is improvable; a different period, area and method, so not a replication of the challenge.
